entries.headline: Baseline: 4 enacted changes take effect Oct 1, 2026 (RI, NE, CT, MD); 3 bills still pending (PA, NY, IL)
entries.summary: First check. Only Rhode Island's 10/1 law changes a warranty labor rule for Subaru-line passenger vehicles, and the site already applies it through the date selector. Nebraska, Connecticut and Maryland changes are scope or procedure. Kentucky's July law affects Class 7+ heavy trucks only. Pennsylvania SB 1182 is the one to watch: it would bring service contracts and CPO into Pennsylvania's reimbursement rules if the House acts before the session ends 11/30/2026.

items.status: Signed by Governor 06/22/2026 (S 2347 Sub A = Chapter 180; H 8213 Sub A = Chapter 179); takes effect 10/01/2026
items.summary_short: Amends R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.1-6 and related sections. Warranty labor is paid at the dealer's non-warranty labor rate multiplied by the ACTUAL time the technician worked.
items.summary: Amends R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.1-6 and related sections. Warranty labor is paid at the dealer's non-warranty labor rate multiplied by the ACTUAL time the technician worked. That time is shown by the technician's time punch, includes diagnostic and manufacturer tech-assist time, and must come with a dealer attestation. It is the first actual-time rule in the country for all line-makes. Named items paid at the dealer's retail rate now include CPO warranty issued by the manufacturer, distributor, factory branch, common entity or agent. Other changes: duties extend to distributors and factory branches; dealers get at least 90 days to submit claims; the manufacturer has 45 days to approve or disapprove, with a written explanation; dealers get 45 days to resubmit. The manufacturer bears the burden of proof when it disapproves based on technician time. Chargebacks are allowed within 12 months for false or unsubstantiated claims. Cost-recovery surcharges are barred. Extended warranties and service contracts are not named. Status confirmed on status.rilegislature.gov: both bills were signed 6/22/2026. Section 2 of each act sets the 10/1/2026 effective date.
items.atlas_impact: Already reflected: date selector switches RI to actual technician time and CPO Required on 10/1/2026.

items.status: Passed 48-1-0 on 04/10/2026; approved by Governor 04/14/2026. Sec. 84 makes Sec. 70 operative 10/01/2026.
items.summary_short: Sec. 70 adds § 60-1438(7): 'This section does not apply to recreational vehicles.' RVs move to the new Recreational Vehicle Industry Regulation Act. A word diff of Sec.
items.summary: Sec. 70 adds § 60-1438(7): 'This section does not apply to recreational vehicles.' RVs move to the new Recreational Vehicle Industry Regulation Act. A word diff of Sec. 70 against the current § 60-1438 text on nebraskalegislature.gov found no other change, so the passenger-car warranty rules from LB667 (2025) stay the same. For Subaru this is scope housekeeping, not a change in substance.
items.atlas_impact: Scope only (RVs removed). No change to passenger-vehicle cells.

items.status: Signed by Governor 05/27/2026 (per the cga.ct.gov bill status page); §§ 20-25 effective 10/01/2026
items.summary_short: New § 22 covers used vehicles in a dealer's inventory that are under a stop-sale or do-not-drive order for a federal safety or emissions recall.
items.summary: New § 22 covers used vehicles in a dealer's inventory that are under a stop-sale or do-not-drive order for a federal safety or emissions recall. If no remedy or parts are available within 30 days, the franchisor must pay at least 1% of the vehicle's average trade-in value per month, capped at the vehicle's value. Per the OLR summary, an OEM may instead pay through a national recall compensation program of at least equal value, or by agreement. It may not offset these payments through chargebacks or incentive reductions. § 23 amends § 42-133s(j) so these claims follow the existing rules: 30-day approval/deemed approval, payment within 30 days, 1-year audit/chargeback window, and no denial for clerical errors. §§ 20-21 and 25 cover facility alterations and definitions; § 24 covers consumer data. The labor rate (§ 42-133s(c)) and time allowances are unchanged.
items.atlas_impact: Claim rules extend to stop-sale compensation claims. Labor rate and time cells unchanged.

items.summary_short: Procedural, with an indirect effect on warranty. A dealer association or manufacturer association may request an MVA administrative hearing to resolve a dispute or to get an interpretation of the franchise law, which includes the § 15-212 warranty rules.
items.summary: Procedural, with an indirect effect on warranty. A dealer association or manufacturer association may request an MVA administrative hearing to resolve a dispute or to get an interpretation of the franchise law, which includes the § 15-212 warranty rules. A manufacturer, distributor or factory branch with no franchised dealer in Maryland may not request a hearing. It does not change the § 15-212 rate, time or claim rules. It does open a route for association-level challenges to warranty policies.
items.atlas_impact: Procedural (association hearings). No change to § 15-212 cells.

items.bill: 2026 HB 648 (2026 Ky. Acts ch. 83), amending KRS 190.046
items.status: Signed by Governor 04/10/2026 (Acts Ch. 83); the official KRS 190.046 page shows 'Effective: July 15, 2026'
items.summary_short: Rewrites KRS 190.046(2)(d) for vehicles in Class 7 and above (49 C.F.R. 565.15, heavy trucks) and makes component manufacturers liable. Parts are paid at acquisition cost plus a 30% gross margin.
items.summary: Rewrites KRS 190.046(2)(d) for vehicles in Class 7 and above (49 C.F.R. 565.15, heavy trucks) and makes component manufacturers liable. Parts are paid at acquisition cost plus a 30% gross margin. Labor hours actually incurred by a trained or certified technician are the basis of compensation unless the manufacturer proves by clear and convincing evidence that they were unreasonable; labor guides alone are not enough. It also reimburses training, warranty administration, and diagnostic tools and special tools, and sets a minimum 90-day claim-submission window for Class 7+. For all line-makes, § 190.046(5)(a) now bars requiring claims for sales or service promotion events sooner than 90 days after eligibility. Light-duty warranty rules are unchanged, so for Subaru the only live change is the promotion-claim window.
items.atlas_impact: Class 7+ heavy trucks only; noted in KY record. Light-duty cells unchanged.

items.status: Passed Senate 50-0 on 06/30/2026; referred to House COMMERCE Committee 07/01/2026; no House action since. The 2025-26 session ends 11/30/2026 and the bill dies if not enacted.
items.summary_short: Would amend Board of Vehicles Act § 307 to expressly cover extended warranty, CPO warranty, manufacturer-sponsored maintenance programs, parts-exchange programs and 'a service contract issued by a manufacturer or distributor or its common entity'.
items.summary: Would amend Board of Vehicles Act § 307 to expressly cover extended warranty, CPO warranty, manufacturer-sponsored maintenance programs, parts-exchange programs and 'a service contract issued by a manufacturer or distributor or its common entity'. Parts would be paid at the dealer's retail rate, using the lesser of 100 sequential or 90 days of customer-pay ROs within 180 days. Labor would be paid at the dealer's 'effective nonwarranty labor rate' times the OEM warranty time allowance. That rate is customer labor dollars on qualifying ROs divided by the hours the OEM's warranty time guide would allow for the same repairs. The rebuttal standard changes from 'unreasonable' to 'materially inaccurate', with the burden on the manufacturer. Takes effect 60 days after enactment.
items.atlas_impact: Watch only. If enacted, PA service-contract and CPO cells would change.

items.status: A8773 passed the Assembly 06/01/2026, went to the Senate and was referred to Senate RULES the same day. S8360 has been in Senate TRANSPORTATION since 01/07/2026. The Senate has not acted; the bills die 12/31/2026.
items.summary_short: Would amend VTL § 465 to cover affiliates and subsidiaries and to list 'extended service contract repairs', 'component part warranties' and 'any other franchisor compensated repairs'.
items.summary: Would amend VTL § 465 to cover affiliates and subsidiaries and to list 'extended service contract repairs', 'component part warranties' and 'any other franchisor compensated repairs'. Time allowances would come from the dealer's retail (third-party) labor time guide. Where no guide time exists, OEM time x 1.5 would apply; where no time exists in either, documented actual time. Takes effect immediately.
items.atlas_impact: Watch only. If enacted, NY paid-hours rules would add 1.5× and actual-time fallbacks.

items.bill: SB1939 (104th GA), as amended by Senate Floor Amendments 1-2
items.status: Passed Senate 55-0 on 04/10/2025. In the House it was re-assigned to the Rules Committee on 03/20/2026. It could move in the fall veto session (House session days Nov 17-19 and Dec 1-3, 2026) or the lame-duck session before the 104th GA ends in January 2027.
items.summary_short: Mainly a direct-sales ban: an OEM not licensed to sell direct before 1/1/2022 may not own or operate a dealership or sell direct. It also amends 815 ILCS 710/6.
items.summary: Mainly a direct-sales ban: an OEM not licensed to sell direct before 1/1/2022 may not own or operate a dealership or sell direct. It also amends 815 ILCS 710/6. The underscored text in SA 1 adds a 'routine maintenance' definition used to exclude items from the dealer's average parts-markup calculation: oil and fluids, filters, ICE batteries, bulbs, brake pads, rotors, fasteners, tire/wheel work including alignments and rotations, and accessory installation. It also changes the parts-price comparison group to 'franchises of the same line make'. The existing 1.5x OEM-time fallback, pay for TAC time and the cost-recovery surcharge ban stay.
items.atlas_impact: Watch only. Mostly a direct-sales bill; parts-markup maintenance definition would change.

items.bill: H4019 (194th General Court), 'An Act to ensure fair compensation for warranty service labor'
items.status: Accompanied a study order (see H5320) on 04/02/2026, which means it is effectively dead. Formal sessions ended 07/31/2026.
items.summary_short: Would have let dealers base warranty labor time on aftermarket or retail time guides. Hearing held 02/04/2026 before the Joint Committee on Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure.
items.summary: Would have let dealers base warranty labor time on aftermarket or retail time guides. Hearing held 02/04/2026 before the Joint Committee on Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure.

entries.method: Official legislature sites, checked 2026-09-25: RI bill-status report (status.rilegislature.gov, S2347/H8213) and public-law chapters 179/180; the NE LB972 bill page and slip law, with Sec. 84 operative dates and a word diff of Sec. 70 against the current § 60-1438; CT SB 413 bill status, PA 26-24 text and OLR public act summary; the PA SB 1182 bill page (palegis.us) and PN 1866 text; NY A8773/S8360 actions on nyassembly.gov and the A8773 text; the IL SB1939 bill status and Senate Amendment 1 markup (ilga.gov); the KY HB 648 record page and the KRS 190.046 official PDF; MD SB 345 (mgaleg); MA H4019 history (malegislature.gov); CA leginfo code pages for §§ 3064-3065.25, a 2025-26 full-text bill search for 3065.1/3065.2/3065.25/3065.3/3065.4, the Governor's 9/20/2026 legislative update, the NMVB 7/16/2026 meeting packet and the 2026 Assembly calendar; the MI MCL page and official bill search; the MN revisor; the WI statutes; FL 2026 Statutes; VA LIS; the OH Revised Code; and the IL House 2026 veto-session calendar. Web searches covered other 2026 warranty-reimbursement bills in MI, OH, NJ, MA, TX, FL, GA, NC, WI, MN, CO, NH and others. Only items confirmed on an official site are listed as enacted or pending. Baseline 'no change' results for the remaining states come from the 9/24-25 atlas research (all_states.json effective_notes). Limitations: ilsos.gov (Illinois MVRB) and autonews.com (paywall/403) could not be read, and the Ohio legislature search is JS-rendered.
